key_insight: Active learning makes machine-learning interatomic potentials more data-efficient by selecting reference calculations relevant to their intended simulation conditions.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive training can support atomistic modeling of mechanics, diffusion, functional materials, and reactive systems while targeting costly reference calculations where needed.
method: Generate candidate atomic configurations and select informative samples.
Run reference calculations, update the potential, and repeat.
Use uncertainty-, representation-, or reaction-aware selection, including workflows with pretrained models.
evidence_signal: The review surveys more than 70 studies, emphasizing 2020–2026, across diverse materials and simulation tasks rather than reporting a single benchmark.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates differ across model architectures and can be least reliable in the unfamiliar regimes where trustworthy selection matters most.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
